correctness.rationale: For J(n,2), n>=5, averaging over permutations of n-3 unused labels followed by transposition-odd antisymmetrization preserves the fixed-edge objective and does not increase the adjacency commutator norm. The resulting full commutator exchanges parity subspaces; its negative-mode Gram decomposes into the 2x2 matrix [[A,sqrt(m)B],[sqrt(m)B,C]] and the repeated scalar (2m+2)t², where m=n-3, A=6+3m-2mt+mt², C=m-2mt+(7m+2)t², B=-2+8t-2t². C minus repeated scalar=m(1-2t+5t²)>0, so the larger 2x2 eigenvalue Φ_m is exactly the squared norm. The positive definite coefficient of t² yields strong convexity and a unique minimizer; d_edge=2/sqrt(min Φ_m). The m→∞ crossing of q1=3-2t+t² and q2=1-2t+7t² at t=1/sqrt(3) produces a sharp m^-1/2 leading distance and negative m^-1 avoided-crossing correction. Independent full adjacency-matrix commutator norms matched Φ for n=5..10 and five rational/real test values per n, and asymptotic numerical controls for m=100,1000,10000 matched analytic convergence; these finite checks do not establish all n.
